Rashi on Nedarim 27a:1:1.english: Benot shuaḥ - Benot sheva [a variety of fig].

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:1:2.hebrew: הייתי אומר תאנים שחורות ולבנות אסורין - דהיינו פלוני ופלוני, ובנות שוח מותרות, דהיינו נמי מין תאנים. והיינו נדר שהותר מקצתו ומקצתו אסור, דתאנים אסורות ובנות שוח מותרות:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:1:2.english: I would have said [that] black and white figs are forbidden - That is, such-and-such [types], and benot shuaḥ are permitted, which are also a species of fig. And this is a vow that was partially dissolved while part of it [remains] forbidden, since [the] figs are forbidden and [the] benot shuaḥ are permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:1:3.hebrew: ורבי עקיבא היא - כדקתני, עד שבא ר' עקיבא ולימד וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:1:3.english: And it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Akiva - As it teaches: "until Rabbi Akiva came and taught," etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:1:4.hebrew: ופליגי רבנן עליה - דאמרי הכלכלה אסורה ובנות שוח מותרות, וקשיא לרבא, דאמר דכולי עלמא היכא דאמר פלוני ופלוני אסורין ואבא מותר, דכולן מותרין דברי הכל:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:1:4.english: And the Rabbis disagree with him - For they say [that] the basket is forbidden and the benot shuaḥ are permitted, and [this] poses a difficulty for Rava, who says [that] everyone agrees [that] where one said, "So-and-so and So-and-so are forbidden, and [my] father is permitted," all of them are permitted according to all opinions.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:2:1.hebrew: תריץ לה באומר הייתי אומר כל הכלכלה אסורה ובנות שוח מותרות - היינו דומיא דכולכם אסורין חוץ מאבא דפליגי, ור' עקיבא היא ולא רבנן:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:2:1.english: He resolves it as [referring to] one who says, "I would have said [that] the entire basket is forbidden and the benot shuaḥ are permitted" - This is similar to [the case of] "You are all forbidden except for my father," where they disagree, and it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Akiva and not [that of] the Rabbis.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:3:1.hebrew: נדר מחמשה בני אדם הותר א' מהן - כגון דאמר: "פלוני ופלוני אסורין ופלוני מותר", הותרו כולן:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:3:1.english: [If one] vowed [not to benefit] from five people, [and] one of them was permitted - For example, where he said, "So-and-so and so-and-so are forbidden, and so-and-so is permitted," all of them are permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:3:2.hebrew: חוץ מאחד מהם - דהיינו דומיא ד"כולכם אסורים חוץ מאבא", הוא מותר וכולן אסורין. והכי איכא למשמע מינה, דהך סיפא ב"כולכם" קמיירי — מדקתני "חוץ", משמע דאמר "כולכם"; ומדסיפא קמיירי ב"כולכם", לא פליגי אלא ב"לזה ולזה":
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:3:2.english: Except for one of them - That is similar to [the case of] "All of you are forbidden except for my father," [where] he is permitted and all of them are forbidden. And thus one can infer from it that this latter clause speaks of [a case where he said] "all of you" — since it teaches "except for," it implies that he said "all of you"; and since the latter clause speaks of "all of you," they only disagree regarding [a case where he said] "to this one and to this one."

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:4:1.hebrew: רישא - דקתני הותר לאחד מהן הותרו כולן, ר' עקיבא היא ולא רבנן, דלרבי עקיבא נדר שהותר מקצתו הותר כולו:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:4:1.english: The first clause - Which teaches: "[If the vow] was dissolved for one of them, all of them are dissolved," is [in accordance with] Rabbi Akiva and not the Rabbis, for according to Rabbi Akiva, a vow that is partially dissolved is completely dissolved.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:4:2.hebrew: וסיפא - דקתני הוא מותר והן אסורין, דברי הכל היא. והכא נמי קאמר רבה דבכולכם כולן אסורות, דברי הכל (היא):
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:4:2.english: And the latter clause - where it teaches [that] he is permitted and they are forbidden, is [the opinion of] everyone. And here too, Rabbah says that in [the case of] "to all of you," all of them are forbidden [according to] everyone.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:4:3.hebrew: ואי לרבא - אמר לזה ולזה דברי הכל מותר, ובכולכם פליגי: רישא דקמיירי בלזה ולזה — דברי הכל, דהכי נמי אמר דלזה ולזה ד"ה מותר. וסיפא — הוא מותר והן אסורין — רבנן היא, דרבא לטעמיה, דאמר בכולכם פליגי ורבנן אוסרים. מ"מ, בין לרבא בין לרבה, רישא בלזה ולזה וסיפא בכולכם:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:4:3.english: And if [it is explained] according to Rava - [who] said [that regarding] "to this one and to this one" everyone agrees [it is] permitted, and regarding "all of you" they disagree: the first clause, which deals with "to this one and to this one," is [in accordance with] everyone's opinion, for so too did [Rava] say, that [regarding] "to this one and to this one" everyone agrees [it is] permitted. And the latter clause — [where the ruling is that] he is permitted and they are forbidden — is [in accordance with] the Rabbis, for Rava follows his own reasoning, as he said that regarding "all of you" they disagree and the Rabbis forbid [them]. In any event, both according to Rava and according to Rabbah, the first clause [deals] with "to this one and to this one," and the latter clause with "all of you."

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:5:1.english: And he became sick - [This refers to] the one who imposed the vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:6:1.hebrew: דאתפיס זכוותא - שהביא שטרי זכיותיו לב"ד, והיה צריך לחזור לביתו:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:6:1.english: Who deposited [documents of] merit - For he brought his documents of merit to the court, and he needed to return to his home.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:6:2.hebrew: ואמר - לב"ד ולבעל דינו: אי לא אתינא וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:6:2.english: And he said - to the court and to his opponent: "If I do not come, etc."

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:7:1.english: But unto the damsel you shall do nothing - Because she was coerced.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:8:1.hebrew: וכי תימא קטלא שאני - דגבי קטלא חס רחמנא עלה כי אניסה, אבל בשאר אונסין דליכא חיוב קטלא, לא מפטר משום אונס:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:8:1.english: And if you would say [that] death is different - For regarding death, the Merciful One had compassion on her when she was forced; but in other cases of unavoidable circumstances, where there is no liability for death, one is not exempted on account of unavoidable circumstances.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:8:2.english: But didn’t we learn, etc. - And he is exempt [from his vow].

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:9:1.english: And according to Rava - Who says [that] he is constrained by unavoidable circumstances and is exempt.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:9:2.hebrew: מאי שנא מהא דתנן וכו' - דכי מת בתוך שנים עשר חודש, דאע"ג דאנסיה מיתה, הוי גט ופטורה מן הייבום:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:9:2.english: How is it different from that which we learned, etc. - For when he died within twelve months, even though death constrained him, it is a [valid] bill of divorce and she is exempt from levirate marriage.

Rashi on Nedarim 27a:9:3.hebrew: אמרי - משום הכי הוי גט, אע"פ שמת בתוך הזמן:
Rashi on Nedarim 27a:9:3.english: They say - For this reason it is a [valid] bill of divorce, even though he died within the [allotted] time.

Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:2:1.hebrew: לא באומר אילו הייתי יודע שבנות שוח בתוכה הייתי אומר כל הכלכלה אסורה וכו' - וא"ת: מ"ש גבי בצל דס"ד דמקשה שאמר "הייתי אומר כל הבצלים", וגבי כלכלה ס"ד דמחשבינן דאמר "שחורות", וכל חד דחייה לזה ולזה? וי"ל: דגבי בצל משמע בצל סתמא, ולכך משמע כל הבצלים; אבל גבי כלכלה, לא אמר "כל הכלכלה", אלא "כלכלה" בלא "כל", והרי לא נדר מן הכלכלה עצמה — שאינה ראויה לאכילה — אלא ממה שבתוכה נדר, ולכך ס"ד דאמר "הייתי אומר תאנים שחורות וכו'". ואית דגרסי בברייתא: "לא הייתי נודר אלא משאר כלכלה". והשתא ניחא, דמשאר משמע קצת שמפרש "תאנים שחורות ולבנות וכו'":
Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:2:1.english: No, [it is speaking] of one who says: Had I known that benot shuaḥ were in it, I would have said, "The entire basket is forbidden, etc." - And if you ask: What is the difference regarding an onion, where the questioner's initial assumption was that he said, "I would have said all onions [are forbidden]," whereas regarding a basket, the initial assumption was that we consider him to have said "black [and white figs]," and [the Gemara] deflected each one [in the opposite direction] — this one to that, and that one to this? And one can say [in resolution]: Regarding an onion, [his vow] implies an unspecified onion, and therefore it implies all onions. However, regarding a basket, he did not say "the entire basket," but rather "a basket" without [the word] "all," and indeed he did not vow [to prohibit himself] from the basket itself — since it is not fit for eating — rather, he vowed from what is inside it; and therefore we initially assumed that he said, "I would have said black figs, etc." And there are those who have the reading in the baraita: "I would not have vowed except from the rest of the basket." And now it is well [understood], for from "the rest of" it is somewhat implied that he is specifying "black and white figs, etc."

Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:4:1.hebrew: אי לרבה רישא כרבי עקיבא וכו' - דנדר א' מחמשה משמע שהיה מונה והולך עד חמשה, והיינו דאמר "פלוני ופלוני"; ואחזרה קאי, שקאמר בסוף: "הייתי אומר פלוני ופלוני". וסיפא, דקתני "חוץ מאחד מהם" — היינו שהותר בלשון זה, שאמר בסוף: "הייתי אומר כולכם חוץ מאביו". ולכך קאמר דלרבה הוי רישא כר"ע דווקא, ושרי ב"פלוני ופלוני", וסיפא דאסר ב"כולכם חוץ מאביו" מיתוקמא ואפילו כדברי הכל. דלרבא רישא דברי הכל, כדקתני איהו לעיל דהכל מודים ב"פלוני ופלוני", וסיפא רבנן דוקא, דאסרי ב"כולכם", ורבי עקיבא שרי; והלכך לדידיה רבנן קתני לה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:4:1.english: If [it is] according to Rabbah, the first clause is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, etc. - For [the phrase] "he vowed [concerning] one of five" implies that he was enumerating them one after another up to five, and this is [the case] where he says "So-and-so and So-and-so"; and it refers to the retraction, where he says at the end, "I would have said, 'So-and-so and So-and-so.'" And the latter clause, which teaches "except for one of them" — this is where [the vow] was dissolved with this wording, that he said at the end, "I would have said, 'All of you except his father.'" And therefore [the Gemara] says that according to Rabbah, the first clause is specifically in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who permits [all of them] in [the case of] "So-and-so and So-and-so," whereas the latter clause, where he forbids [the rest] in [the case of] "all of you except his father," can be established even as everyone's opinion. Whereas according to Rava, the first clause is everyone's opinion — as he himself stated above, that all agree in [the case of] "So-and-so and So-and-so" — and the latter clause is specifically the Rabbis, who forbid [the rest] in [the case of] "all of you," while Rabbi Akiva permits [them]; and therefore, according to him, the Rabbis taught it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:6:1.english: His favorable [documents] in court - [This means] a document of entitlement.

Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:7:1.hebrew: והא אונס רחמנא פטריה - וה"נ לא הוצרך להתנות עליו, דדבר פשוט הוא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:7:1.english: But the Merciful One exempted a victim of unavoidable circumstances - And here too, he did not need to stipulate regarding it [i.e., unavoidable circumstances], for it is an obvious matter.

Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:8:1.hebrew: וכי תימא קטלא שאני - אבל הכא לעולם הוי פושע ממה שלא התנה להוציא אונס מן הכלל — הא תנן: "אלו הן נדרי אונסין", ולא אמרינן איבעי לאיתנויי; הכא נמי לא שנא. וא״ת: באיזה אונס מיירי? הא באונסא דשכיח איבעי ליה לאיתנויי; אי נמי אונס דשכיח ולא שכיח — הא נמי איבעי לאיתנויי ולא אתני, כדמוכח בכתובות גבי גט, ובשמעתין מדמה ליה לגיטין! וי״ל: דמיירי באונס דלא שכיח כלל. וא״ת: א״כ דמיירי באונס דלא שכיח כלל, מאי טעמיה דרב הונא דאמר דליבטלן זכותיה? והא אונס דלא שכיח כלל לא איבעי לאתנויי, כדמוכח בגיטין פרק מי שאחזו (גיטין דף עג -) גבי נפל מן הגג! וי״ל: דשאני הכא דאמר ליבטלן זכוותיה משום שמודה שהשטר פסול, לכך אמר ליבטלן זכוותיה אפי' באונס דלא שכיח, דהודאת בעל דין כמאה עדים דמי; והא מודה שראיותיו שקר הן, שהרי אינו מוחל לו שום דבר, אלא מטעם הודאה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 27a:8:1.english: And if you would say that [the penalty of] death is different - but here he is always [considered] negligent because he did not stipulate to exclude unavoidable accident from the rule — behold, we learned [in the Mishnah]: "These are vows of unavoidable accident," and we do not say he should have stipulated; here too, there is no difference. And if you will ask: To which [type of] unavoidable accident does [the Mishnah] refer? For in the case of a common unavoidable accident, he should have stipulated; alternatively, [in the case of] an unavoidable accident that is [sometimes] common and [sometimes] uncommon, in that [case] too he should have stipulated and did not stipulate, as is proven in Ketubot regarding a bill of divorce, and in our sugya [the Gemara] compares it to bills of divorce! And one can answer: That [the Mishnah] refers to an unavoidable accident that is not common at all. And if you will ask: If so, that [our sugya too] refers to an unavoidable accident that is not common at all, what is the reason of Rav Huna, who says that his rights should be voided? For in [the case of] an unavoidable accident that is not common at all, he did not need to stipulate, as is proven in Gittin, chapter Mi She'achazo (Gittin 73a) regarding one who fell from the roof! And one can answer: That it is different here, where [Rav Huna] says his rights should be voided, because he admits that the document is invalid; therefore [Rav Huna] said his rights should be voided even in [the case of] an unavoidable accident that is not common, for a litigant's admission is like [the testimony of] a hundred witnesses; and here he admits that his proofs are false, since he does not waive anything to him, rather [it is] on account of admission.
